text:
Anna P.: quick sync — infra needs a concrete ingest contract for the KV + prefix cache effectiveness signals so Console can ship the segmented dashboard. top-line metrics we need: hit_rate, eviction_rate, reuse_by_workload, and prefetch/warmth ratio. also want tenant attribution and sampling hints.
Ryan K.: +1. can infra emit both per-tenant and aggregated series? the rollup window matters (1m/5m/1h). what's Console's expected cardinality? :thinking_face:
Anna P.: Console wants per-model and per-tenant for the first phase, then aggregate by workload type (embeddings, chat, batch). target cardinality: tens of thousands of tenants but we should sample heavy tail. 
Samira J.: technical constraints from runtime: we can export the following atomics from the runtime: kv_hits, kv_misses, prefix_hits, prefix_insertions, evictions, reuse_count, prefetch_attempts, prefetch_successes. We need naming conventions.
Kelly M.: Can we standardize on metric names and labels? propose:
```
redwood.kv.hits{tenant,model,workload,model_variant}  # counter
redwood.kv.misses{...}  # counter
redwood.kv.evictions{...}  # counter
redwood.prefix.hits{...}  # counter
redwood.prefetch.attempts{...}  # counter
redwood.prefetch.successes{...}  # counter
redwood.reuse.count{...}  # counter (reuse by workload)
```
Ryan K.: Looks good. we also need gauge-ish derived ratios (hit_rate, prefetch_success_rate) at ingest or on-dashboard? I'd prefer derived on the dashboard to keep metric cardinality lower.
Anna P.: Console prefers ingest of raw counters and let Grafana/Platform compute ratios. We do want one precomputed gauge: `cache.warmth_estimate{tenant,model}` sampled 5m so UX can show quick heatmap without heavy query cost. would runtime produce that?
Samira J.: runtime can emit a `cache.warmth_estimate` gauge sampled 5m computed from recent access patterns and prefix KV reuse heuristics. caveat: it's approximate and non-monotonic. include `window=5m` label? probably not — keep as metric with implicit sampling.
Kelly M.: For evictions we need reason labels: `eviction_reason=memory_pressure|ttl|manual` so Console can filter. Also add `cache_tier=kv|prefix` dimension.
Infra-Bot: new issue created: infra/telemetry#412 - define ingest contract for cache effectiveness metrics (assigned: @samira).
Anna P.: sampling plan: heavy tenants (top 1%) ingest full label sets. medium tenants: sample labels model_variant only. small tenants: aggregate-only ingest. can infra add `ingest_sampling` tag per tenant?
Ryan K.: yes, we can add a `ingest_sampling=tier_full|tier_medium|tier_agg` label emitted by the sidecar at the point of scrape. make default `tier_agg`.
Samira J.: follow-up Q: retention SLAs? Console wants 90d for heatmaps, 365d for aggregate monthly ROI. storing full-cardinality counters for 365d is expensive. propose: roll high-cardinality to rolled-up aggregates after 30d.
Kelly M.: agree. UI will fallback to rollups after 30d. we need explicit retention labels and a lifecycle doc so SREs can plan storage and cost.
Anna P.: someone from DashOps pick up a stub dashboard prototype? DashOps: can you do a first-pass wireframe with these metrics and sample queries? :eyes:
DashOps: will do. I can mock a 3-panel layout: 1) global hit/eviction trends, 2) heatmap by tenant (warmth_estimate), 3) reuse attribution by workload. ETA EOD tomorrow.
Ryan K.: telemetry ingest notes: prefer prometheus-style exposition on the runtime sidecar plus a push proxy for private deployments. also add a small JSON schema for the ingest contract so teams can validate.
Samira J.: i'll draft the JSON schema and the prom metric name table. will include examples for multi-tenant labels and for the `ingest_sampling` behaviors.
Anna P.: ok next steps: 1) Samira: PR with names + schema by Tue; 2) Infra: confirm retention/cost plan and sampling enforcement; 3) DashOps: wireframe EOD tomorrow; 4) Platform Console: prepare dashboard placeholders and fallback UX notes. Everyone ack?
Kelly M.: ack.
Ryan K.: ack.
Samira J.: ack, taking ownership of the PR.
Anna P.: thanks all — filing a short RFC doc after this thread. :thumbsup:
